Kriscore Capital led the round alongside Eximius Ventures, with participation from Indigram Labs Foundation and angel investors from the agriculture sector. The company says it will use the capital to expand its product suite, grow its engineering team, and widen its geographical footprint across Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa and India. Agribusinesses in the Global South still run critical operations over WhatsApp messages, phone calls and spreadsheets, so head office systems rarely reflect what is happening on the ground in real time, says India-headquartered Myca. The company’s software takes in the messages, calls and photos field teams already produce, turns them into structured data, and uses AI agents to handle the follow-up work supervisors typically do. It sits on top of a company’s existing ERP and CRM systems rather than replacing them. Use cases include field sales, crop surveys, procurement planning, credit assessment, and warehouse and logistics tracking. The product launched in April in India and Indonesia, and the company says it is now active in eight countries. The package comprises $1.3 million in funding plus $200,000 for technical assistance and business development provided through the Dutch Good Growth Fund (DGGF) , which Triple Jump manages. Unlike traditional accelerators that back founder-led teams, Pyramidia operates as a venture builder : it originates concepts in-house, conducts early pilots, then recruits co-founders to spin the best ideas into independent companies. The approach is designed to compress the riskiest part of company creation while freeing founding teams from time-consuming corporate administration and fundraising so they can focus on product–market fit and scale . Founded in 2021 by Ruth Bertens (ex-McKinsey) and Joseph Rehmann (founder of Victory Farms), Pyramidia targets pain points in Africa’s agri-food systems—water stress, input inefficiency, traceability, and protein supply—where climate resilience and unit economics intersect. The studio’s process borrows globally proven technologies and adapts them to local realities, moving ideas through pilot → build → scale with shared services for finance, legal, data, and field operations. The company does not buy or hold inventory, an asset-light model designed to keep costs and risk low. According to Startups, Vereda operates with its own field team and a network of independent sales agents. The problem, says North Carolina-based startup Upstream Biotechnology, is that genes conferring disease resistance can also impose a yield penalty.
